cluster_summary: These vulnerabilities stem from failures to correctly establish, propagate, or enforce the security context (e.g., document author permissions or restricted mode flags) when processing user-supplied content within macro and rendering pipelines. This leads to unauthorized script execution or privilege escalation. The fixes involve reordering context switches, adding permission checks, propagating restriction flags, or using correct rendering APIs.
guideline_text: Trace lower-privilege script, template, macro, plugin, or API callers that can invoke privileged server-side capabilities into server-side include, template rendering, servlet dispatch, raw object access, internal file reads, or privileged framework APIs. Report code paths where a higher privilege check is not enforced at the API entry point before exposing the server-side capability. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 3 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should check the required higher privilege at the exposed API boundary and return no sensitive result when the caller lacks that privilege.

mechanism.missing_guard: a higher privilege check is not enforced at the API entry point before exposing the server-side capability
mechanism.name: privileged server-side capability exposed to lower privilege context
mechanism.sink_shape: server-side include, template rendering, servlet dispatch, raw object access, internal file reads, or privileged framework APIs
mechanism.source_shape: lower-privilege script, template, macro, plugin, or API callers that can invoke privileged server-side capabilities
mechanism.typical_fix: check the required higher privilege at the exposed API boundary and return no sensitive result when the caller lacks that privilege

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Ensure that content is processed with the security context of its author or intended user, either by reordering context switches, adding explicit authorization checks, or using APIs that automatically use the correct context.
sub_patterns.name: Improper authorization context when processing user-supplied content
sub_patterns.root_cause: The code uses the wrong user or document context (e.g., viewer, document author, or macro author) when parsing or rendering user-supplied content, leading to unauthorized execution of scripts.
